title: Birth in Metairie and first hearing parades
summary: Born February 12, 1929 in Metairie, he moved to New Orleans after the service. He first heard spirited music in parades; nobody in his family played.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Out in Metro, Louisiana. I lived in Metro about, oh, I'd say 22 years or so. And after I'd gotten out of the service, I moved into the city of New Orleans. And I've been living there ever since.
And let's see now. What's your present address, Moose?
4659 Eastern Street. That's in the Gentilly section.
And where were you, when did you first hear any music? When?

Well, that's going to be kind of hard to say, because being in New Orleans, I mean, you're just naturally brought up around music, see. I guess the parades, that's probably the first real spirited music I ever heard, and I took a liking to, you know.
Your mother and father didn't play and hang around the house, or uncles or aunts, anybody
like that? No, as far as I know, I'm about the only one that ever invested $60 in a horn, you know. I'm about the only one that plays anything.
Do you remember any of the parade bands you heard?
Offhand, no. I mean, most of them, I think, might have been high school bands, you know, high school bands from the city.
Not the colored parades? No, no, unfortunately. They don't have a lot of metry very much, I guess, at that, no.

Once in a while you might run up on a good old time guitar player, or maybe fellas that had played years before, you know, they aren't active now, of course, but you might just run up on one every once in a while, you know, and you hear some real good musicians.
